title: When the Group Chat Falls
premise: Ines Oyelaran, a debate champion raised by a Nigerian family that prizes silence over scandal, has spent fifteen years perfecting the art of being careful. When her teacher pairs her with Theo Marchetti—her nemesis and the only person who's ever noticed how tired she is—for a semester-long oral history project, their forced collaboration cracks open a secret: Ines's late grandmother left her an inheritance her parents have hidden, tied to a life they disapprove of. As the project becomes a public audition, Ines must choose between the dutiful daughter she's performed and the self her grandmother believed in, even if telling the truth costs her both her parents' approval and her fragile new love with Theo. She wins the argument at last—not on a stage, but at home—and ends the book choosing herself, with Theo beside her.
about_author: Ada Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former high-school debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers say true things in competition and lie everywhere else. She writes from a small apartment full of annotated transcripts and cold coffee.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet Ines mid-debate, flawless on stage and silent at home, where her parents' rules about gratitude and reputation govern everything—including the locked box of her grandmother's belongings she's never been allowed to open. When Ms. Ferreira pairs her with Theo Marchetti for the semester oral history project, Ines's careful world tilts. Emotional beat: suffocating order, first crack of disruption.

chapters.title: Nemesis Theory
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced together after school, Ines and Theo trade barbs until Theo admits he's always watched her because she looks like someone holding her breath. Interviewing neighborhood elders for the project, Ines finds her grandmother's name in an old recording—a woman who chose love over duty and was erased for it. Emotional beat: antagonism melting into recognition; the past surfacing.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Left
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines opens the locked box: letters, a ring, proof of the inheritance her parents buried to keep her on their path. Confronting them detonates the house; her mother calls it betrayal, her father calls it grief. Meanwhile Theo, exposed as the son of the man her grandmother loved, becomes collateral damage, and Ines pushes him away to protect him. Emotional beat: rupture on every front; lowest point.

chapters.title: The Final Audition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The project's public showcase forces Ines to present—or to tell the truth about what inheritance really means. She abandons the safe script, tells her grandmother's story and her own, and asks Theo, in front of everyone, to stop being her nemesis. Her mother, listening from the back row, doesn't forgive—but doesn't look away either. Emotional beat: catharsis, chosen identity, love claimed against duty.
